extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, criminal-justice advocates, researchers, and informed members of the public interested in criminal justice reform
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and principles for evaluating and designing criminal justice policies and reforms aimed at reducing incarceration, protecting individual rights, and improving public safety. Focuses on evidence, equity, funding use, conditions, and reentry supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair and equitable criminal justice system
rubrics_metrics.description: A fair and equitable criminal justice system is critical for a healthy democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Brennan Center champions reforms that protect individual rights and public safety; policy work should pursue an affirmative vision of a better system for everyone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Champion evidence-based reforms that protect both individual rights and public safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy proposals and advocacy should be grounded in empirical research and rigorous data rather than political rhetoric or myths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bipartisan solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Find bipartisan solutions that safeguard human rights and promote safer communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts should prioritize approaches that can gain cross-party support to create durable reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address racial and economic inequities
rubrics_metrics.description: Address racial and economic inequities that are embedded in the criminal justice system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reform strategies should explicitly target disparities and ensure policy changes reduce unequal harms across communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground debates in accurate data
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground debates in accurate data to counter false narratives used to justify overly punitive policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reliable crime statistics and research to evaluate policy impacts and to rebut myths promoted by politicians and pundits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement effective policies that improve people’s lives
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement effective policies that will improve people’s lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy design should prioritize tangible improvements in outcomes (safety, stability, opportunities) for individuals and communities affected by the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smarter policing and sentencing policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue smarter policing and sentencing policies as part of reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reforms should focus on approaches to policing and sentencing that reduce unnecessary punishment while maintaining public safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humane prison and jail conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve conditions for both staff and those who are incarcerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better environments can lead to better post-release outcomes; policies should ensure humane treatment and safe conditions in facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive reentry programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide supportive reentry programs for people leaving incarceration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reentry supports are part of reducing recidivism and improving long-term outcomes — policy must include services that help people succeed after release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Better federal funding use to reduce incarceration
rubrics_metrics.description: Reform how federal criminal justice funding is used to help cut prison populations while supporting safer communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal dollars should be redirected or structured to incentivize decarceration and community-based safety strategies rather than fueling incarceration growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut jail and prison populations when public safety allows
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the nearly 2 million incarcerated people in the United States would pose no public safety risk if released; work to reduce the number of people in jails and prisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies should identify populations who can be safely released or diverted and implement measures to reduce unnecessary incarceration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for social and economic harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the enormous social and economic costs of the criminal justice system for formerly incarcerated individuals, their families, and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy evaluation should include downstream harms (employment, housing, family stability) and pursue reforms that mitigate these harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent crime, reduce recidivism, and save money
rubrics_metrics.description: A federal agenda should take targeted measures to prevent crime, reduce incarceration and recidivism, and save money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy packages should aim for co-benefits: improving public safety outcomes while reducing corrections costs and reliance on incarceration.
